item.title: PSG rocked as Khvicha Kvaratskhelia suffers season-ending ACL injury
item.description: European champions Paris Saint-Germain have been rocked by the confirmation that star winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia has ruptured his anterior cruciate ligament (ACL). The French club have confirmed Kvaratskhelia, named Champions League player of the season last campaign after PSG won back-to-back European crowns, will undergo surgery in the coming days. But the injury is likely to rule him out for the rest of the season and is a significant blow to PSG’s hopes of winning a third consecutive Champions League title. The Georgia international was hurt during PSG’s 4-2 win over Barcelona in the Champions League on Tuesday evening and was forced off just before the hour mark. The 25-year-old was unable to put any weight on his right leg as he was helped off the pitch, after appearing to twist his knee. PSG also confirmed that Ousmane Dembele and captain Marquinhos are likely to miss the next several weeks due to thigh injuries. Dembele was forced off in the 19th minute, signalling to the bench as he held the back of his left thigh, before Marquinhos was also substituted due to injury in the second half. More follows

item.title: Fabrizio Ravanelli reveals the biggest problem with this Juventus team
item.description: Fabrizio Ravanelli reveals the biggest problem with this Juventus team Juventus face several problems after their disappointing defeat to Lazio at the weekend, which exposed weaknesses that have troubled the team since the start of the season. Their inconsistent performances have frustrated supporters, but the manner of the latest loss has raised even greater concerns. Luciano Spalletti now faces increased pressure as manager , and his future could become uncertain if results don’t improve in the coming weeks. Although Juventus would prefer to maintain stability, the club may eventually consider a change if the situation continues to deteriorate. Spalletti faces growing pressure at Juventus Juventus players will hope the club continues to support Spalletti, as another managerial change could create further uncertainty within the squad. However, if performances do not improve, the manager could pay the price, leaving some players needing to prove their worth under a new coach. The Bianconeri want to return to competing for major honours, but their current struggles suggest that the problems extend beyond the touchline. Juventus must identify the reasons behind their inconsistent displays if they are to recover their form and meet expectations. Former Juventus striker Fabrizio Ravanelli believes the players themselves must accept responsibility for the situation. He has questioned their mentality and suggested that a lack of personality is contributing to the club’s difficulties. (Photo by Chris Ricco/Getty Images) Ravanelli identifies Juventus’ main problem Speaking via Tuttomercatoweb , Ravanelli argued that too many players were failing to show the character expected of someone representing Juventus. He said: “This team lacks personality above all. Many players seem to be hiding, not wanting the ball. Juve isn’t up to par; so many players haven’t shown they’re worthy of the black and white jersey. Everyone’s to blame; you can’t just point the finger at the coach, the club, or the team. But, from the players’ perspective, I expected something more in terms of pride and inner fire.” Ravanelli’s assessment places responsibility across the club, while emphasising that the players have not demonstrated enough pride or determination. His comments suggest Juventus need more than tactical adjustments to turn their season around.

item.title: Pirates have another offseason trade idea with Astros
item.description: PITTSBURGH, PENNSYLVANIA - MAY 9: General Manager Ben Cherington of the Pittsburgh Pirates looks on during batting practice before the game against the Atlanta Braves at PNC Park on May 9, 2025 in Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania. (Photo by Justin Berl/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Pittsburgh Pirates made a big trade last offseason with the Houston Astros that landed them second baseman Brandon Lowe, outfielder Jake Mangum, and left-handed pitcher Mason Montgomery. All three players made significant contributions for the Pirates in 2026, so it might be in their best interest to make another deal with the team from Space City. Bleacher Report writer Kerry Miller suggests the trade that would send Astros third baseman Isaac Paredes to the Pirates. “Brandon Lowe’s one season with Pittsburgh was everything the Pirates could have asked for, playing in 150 games and hitting 35 home runs. Now he’s a free agent, though, and it’s back to the drawing board with several spots in the lineup that could use an infusion of offense. Third base, in particular, is looking bleak, and we’ve previously mentioned that Houston is probably going to be willing to move one of its infielders. And, come on, “Pittsburgh Paredes” is right there as an awesome nickname,“ Miller wrote. While Paredes has primarily played third base in his first two years with the Astros, he also has experience playing second base. That is where the team might need some reinforcements if Lowe were to walk in free agency. The Astros have a surplus of infielders, with Carlos Correa re-entering the fold after an original trade brought him back to Houston in 2025, when Paredes went down with a long-term injury. It’s a trade that could make sense for both sides if there was interest, so Pittsburgh should at least give Houston another call this offseason. item.title: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers after season-opening win over Knicks
item.description: NEW YORK -- The Philadelphia 76ers opened the 2026-27 season with an impressive 1 06-100 win over the defending champion New York Knicks on the road to spoil their ring night. The Sixers were able to get the job done by locking in defensively in the second half and finding ways to seal possessions with big rebounds. LeBron James, in his Sixers debut, had 14 points, nine rebounds, and seven assists while Jaylen Brown had 19 points, eight rebounds, and six assists in his debut. Tyrese Maxey had 28 points, five assists, four rebounds, three steals, and three blocks while Joel Embiid had 13 points, six assists, and 11 rebounds. VJ Edgecombe added nine points, and Anfernee Simons added 13 points, and Kentavious Caldwell-Pope added 10 points while also making their Sixers debuts. Here are the three biggest takeaways following the win: Maxey's defensive prowess When one thinks of Tyrese Maxey, they think of offense. They think of his ability to knock down tough shots, get to the basket, make plays for others, take games over in the blink of an eye. Not many think of Maxey's defensive work. He impressed in this one as he really sat down and defended on the perimeter to make life tough on New York's guards. He was able to come up with some big time steals and then come up with some impressive blocks. If that keeps up, then that changes things for Philadelphia's chances as it moves forward. "He's a really high IQ player," VJ Edgecombe said of Maxey. "He's obviously, you know, he got that God-given talent where he's so fast, he's athletic, so he's able to catch some blocks, and obviously he's smart. He can read the passing lanes, read it, read the offensive play. He's really good at being in the passing lane. Like I said, it looks like he's running 100 miles per hour because of how fast he is. "It was incredibly huge tonight, because I thought we were generating lots of wide-open 3s and just nobody could throw one in," said coach Nick Nurse. "And those guys kind of broke through on that and moved the scoreboard for us. It’s one of those things, if you’re, again, making the right reads and it’s a kick-out catch-and-shoot three, you’re gonna have to keep taking them all night whether you’re making them or not, and it was good those guys kind of broke the seal a little bit, I thought." Brown gets going in the second half It was a quiet start for Brown in his Sixers debut as he started out missing some easy looks, but as the game wore on, Brown broke out and really gave Philadelphia the offensive punch it needed to keep up with the champs. He was punching the gaps, getting to the basket, making the Knicks adjust to him, and that opened up different opportunities for the Sixers offensively. The two 3s he made in the third--after Simons was able to beak the seal--were huge, including one to beat the buzzer. "Probably a couple things," Nurse said of Brown's night. "Probably our defensive rebounding, if that makes any sense. Gave him a chance to play not necessarily in break, but in transition [in] people moving up the floor. And he’s kind of been able to hit some gaps as everything’s kind of moving, and he just had a nice run of the ball finding him. Him making tough moves to the basket. Ran a couple plays for him. A little bit combination of those things." This article originally appeared on Sixers Wire: 3 biggest takeaways for Sixers after season-opening win over Knicks

item.title: Raya reveals why he chose Arsenal over Bayern Munich
item.description: Raya reveals why he chose Arsenal over Bayern Munich David Raya came close to joining Bayern Munich before signing for Arsenal in the summer of 2023, initially on loan from Brentford. The Spanish goalkeeper had impressed at Brentford and was ready to take the next step in his career. Bayern were looking for a goalkeeper after Manuel Neuer suffered an injury, and Raya emerged as a target. They were the first club to approach him, and the Spaniard was open to joining one of Europe’s leading teams. However, the move failed to materialise, allowing Arsenal to step in and secure his signature despite already having Aaron Ramsdale , who was regarded as one of England’s best goalkeepers at the time. Arteta stood by his decision Arsenal’s decision to sign Raya attracted criticism, with questions raised about bringing in another goalkeeper when Ramsdale was already at the club. Mikel Arteta, however, remained convinced that the Spaniard was the right choice and stood by his decision despite the scrutiny. Raya eventually established himself as Arsenal’s first choice, with his performances helping justify the manager’s faith in him. What initially appeared to be a controversial decision has since become an important part of Arteta’s plans. The goalkeeper could have taken a different path had Bayern completed their pursuit in 2023. Instead, he chose to join Arsenal and continue his career in the Premier League. (Photo by Ryan Pierse/Getty Images) Raya reflects on Bayern interest Raya was asked about the proposed move to Bayern and why it did not happen. Speaking via Football London , he made it clear that his decision was to sign for Arsenal, while stressing that this was not intended as a slight against the German club. “Well, I’m not going to speak about what could have happened or whatnot. “At the end of the day, I chose to sign for Arsenal with no disrespect to Bayern. “It was just the negotiations that we had, but at the end of the day, I signed for Arsenal that year.” Raya’s explanation points to negotiations as the key factor in the transfer failing to materialise. Ultimately, Arsenal secured his services, and Arteta’s confidence in the goalkeeper has been rewarded as Raya established himself as a key figure at the club . _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. The incoming executive will also be expected to begin work as quickly as possible. Frankfurt intend to provide some financial resources for the January transfer window, with additional defensive reinforcements among the squad’s most pressing requirements. The appointment comes at an especially consequential moment for a club attempting to reverse a disappointing domestic trajectory while simultaneously reassessing the business model that helped establish Frankfurt among Germany’s leading clubs. Krösche’s departure brings prolonged uncertainty to an end Krösche’s separation from Frankfurt was officially announced on Sunday, October 18, bringing an end to an association that began in 2021. Although the timing initially came as a surprise, Get German Football News had already reported on the possibility of his departure in late August . At the time, reports of disagreements with returning head coach Adi Hütter had accompanied growing uncertainty surrounding the sporting executive’s position. The recently concluded summer transfer window had also exposed several problems within Frankfurt’s recruitment strategy. A series of developments appear to have contributed to the deterioration of Krösche’s internal standing. His appointment of Albert Riera as head coach earlier this year proved especially contentious. Krösche initially defended the Spaniard following a controversial press conference , but the experiment ultimately failed to produce the desired sporting progress. Hütter’s subsequent return also highlighted changing dynamics within the club’s leadership. According to Kicker , other influential figures within Frankfurt’s organization played significant roles in facilitating the Austrian’s comeback. Meanwhile, Krösche’s discussions with AC Milan during the summer reportedly created additional tensions. The supervisory board was said to have learned of the Italian club’s interest through media reporting rather than directly from the executive. Another controversy concerned a Croatian property transaction involving Krösche and the wife of player agent Andy Bara. Frankfurt conducted internal and external legal reviews that fully cleared Krösche of wrongdoing. Nevertheless, Kicker reports that the failure to inform the supervisory board beforehand contributed to internal dissatisfaction. The increasingly difficult summer transfer window compounded these concerns. Hütter reportedly became frustrated by the delayed acquisition of an experienced defender, while Frankfurt’s unresolved goalkeeping situation also attracted criticism. Ultimately, both Frankfurt and Krösche concluded that an early separation represented the best course of action. Krösche receives emotional farewell from Eintracht supporters Whatever disagreements characterized the closing months of Krösche’s tenure, Monday evening’s general meeting demonstrated the appreciation he had earned during his years in Frankfurt. The 46-year-old delivered an unusually emotional farewell address to approximately 1,300 assembled club members at the Jahrhunderthalle. Krösche acknowledged that his professional demeanor could sometimes make him appear cold or detached. He emphasized, however, that this outward appearance did not reflect his feelings for Frankfurt or the significance of the club’s achievements during his tenure. The departing executive also provided a candid explanation for his decision to step away. After reflecting on his responsibilities and the demands of the position, Krösche said he no longer believed he possessed the necessary drive and effectiveness to perform the role to Frankfurt’s required standards. He explained that a club of Frankfurt’s stature required a sporting executive capable of approaching the job with complete commitment and conviction. Having concluded that he could no longer guarantee this, Krösche approached the supervisory board’s executive committee with his request to leave. His farewell address included affectionate recollections of Frankfurt’s 2022 Europa League triumph, the memorable European encounters with Barcelona, the club’s Champions League adventures and the 2023 DFB-Pokal final. Krösche thanked supporters for the energy and passion they had given him throughout his tenure and promised that he would always remain connected to Eintracht Frankfurt. The assembled members responded by rising to their feet and applauding for almost two minutes. The respectful separation also leaves Krösche free to pursue another professional opportunity. Frankfurt have reportedly secured an agreement requiring his next employer to pay compensation in the region of €4m to €6m. AC Milan remain a possible destination. GGFN reported renewed expectations of Krösche joining the Italian club on Monday , although Kicker subsequently noted that individuals close to the executive expect him to take some time away from football before accepting another position. A remarkable transfer legacy, but not without costly mistakes Krösche leaves Frankfurt having overseen one of the most successful periods in the club’s modern history. The 2022 Europa League triumph naturally represents the sporting highlight, but his tenure also included multiple Champions League qualifications, sustained European involvement and extraordinary revenues generated

item.title: Taylor hails 'electric' Exeter City after Crewe win
item.description: Anthony Scully's first-half penalty set Exeter on the way to beating Crewe [Shutterstock] Exeter City manager Matt Taylor hailed his resurgent side after they inflicted a first league defeat of the season on Crewe Alexandra. The Grecians beat the third-placed Railwaymen 2-0 at St James Park to extend their unbeaten run to four League Two games. Having won just one of their first eight games, Exeter were a point off the relegation places at the end of September. But 10 points from a possible 12 since the start of October has lifted City to 10th place, a point away from the play-off spots. "In terms of our ball use first half we were almost electric, weren't we?" Taylor told BBC Radio Devon. "We looked like we could open the opposition up and get in fantastic attacking areas and positions. "So we're certainly moving in the right direction, but I think that's a month's worth of work on show again. "All of a sudden, if you add the Oxford cup game into it, there's a run of four or five fixtures where we've looked connected as a team, we've looked on the same page and we've improved." Exeter end Crewe's unbeaten run Taylor impressed as Exeter keep another clean sheet Exeter's excellent defensive record was also kept intact in the victory. The Grecians have now conceded just six goals in 12 League Two matches - a record that allowed them to collect points even when they went on a run of four games without scoring in September. Only Bradford City have conceded fewer goals in the EFL this season, having let in five in 11 games. "That's incredible," Taylor said of his side's defensive record. "I'd like that to look the same at the end of the season. "But there will be times when an opposition team opens it up, it's a difficult league and we've worked against some fantastic opposition players and it could have been Crewe tonight. "Going into the game I had a feeling that we were going to play our best attacking game, but it could easily go the other way with how dangerous a team Crewe are. "Full credit to the group that have withstood it again and they can take a lot of confidence from that." All the latest Exeter City news

item.title: ‘These three points will help us’: PSV head coach Peter Bosz happy with Champions League victory over Porto
item.description: ‘These three points will help us’: PSV head coach Peter Bosz happy with Champions League victory over Porto PSV got their Champions League campaign up and running with an important victory away to Porto. Guus Til scored the only goal of the game as the Dutch champions came away from Portugal with all three points and their first win in the Champions League this season. After a defeat last week to RB Leipzig, PSV were desperate to grab a first win in the competition. The victory against Porto now means that PSV have four poitns from three games to start the Champions League, a decent return considering two of their opening three games have been away from home. Speaking to ESPN after the game, head coach Peter Bosz was happy with the result. He said ‘I do think these three points will help us. We took a wrong turn for a moment, but I think we have found our way again’ . Given that the side lost this past weekend to ADO Den Haag, there may have been some concerns that they were not ready for a pretty important Champions League clash with Porto. However, they defended well and Bosz was impressed with the performance of Sven Mijnans. The head coach said ‘I am very curious to see how much he ran. He played very well between the lines, drawing Jan Bednarek away every time and always being available to receive the ball ‘. Next up for PSV in the Champions League is a clash with Belgian champions Club Brugge at home. Before that, however, they have a big Eredivisie game against Feyenoord to contend with. The Rotterdam club have had a blistering start to the domestic campaign and look set to be the biggest rivals PSV have in their bid to regain their title this season. GBeNeFN | Ben Jackson

item.title: Pat Cummins registers unwanted career record as South Africa pull off stunning fightback
item.description: Australia captain Pat Cummins endured a difficult outing with the ball as South Africa mounted a remarkable recovery in the second Test at St George’s Park in Gqeberha, with his figures of 0/96 ranking as the second-most expensive wicketless return of his career. Cummins conceded 96 runs without taking a wicket, better only than his 0/101 against India in Sydney in 2019. The expensive spell came as South Africa recovered from 110-6 to declare at 425-9 on Day 3, putting Australia under pressure after a dramatic turnaround. South Africa’s lower order made the most of the opportunity after the hosts lost their sixth wicket early in the morning session. Captain Temba Bavuma led the fightback with a career-best 179, while Marco Jansen scored 85 and Simon Harmer contributed 82. The recovery was particularly significant in statistical terms. South Africa scored 315 runs after losing their sixth wicket, the second-highest such total in a Test innings. Their effort fell just short of the 318 runs they added against Australia at the Melbourne Cricket Ground in 2008. Australia have also conceded only one higher total after taking the sixth wicket: the 363 runs West Indies scored at Bridgetown in 1955. South Africa's 318-run effort in Melbourne in 2008 is the other entry ahead of the latest Gqeberha performance. The hosts had been in serious trouble at 110-6 after Wiaan Mulder fell for 13 to Mitchell Starc, who claimed his 450th Test wicket. Bavuma and Jansen initially steadied the innings with a 132-run seventh-wicket partnership before Jansen was dismissed by Scott Boland, who finished with 5-81. Harmer then joined Bavuma and the pair added 183 runs for the eighth wicket, turning the innings around. Harmer struck 10 fours and a six in his maiden Test half-century before being bowled by Marnus Labuschagne. Bavuma, meanwhile, reached his fifth Test century off 226 balls and went past his previous best of 172 against West Indies in Johannesburg in 2023. He eventually fell to Starc, bringing the innings to a close soon afterwards. Australia lost Nic Maddinson for a four-ball duck to Kagiso Rabada late in the day and were 3-1 at stumps. Australia won the first Test in Durban by 214 runs and lead the three-match series 1-0. 135086290

item.title: Inzaghi emerges as Juventus option to replace Spalletti in 2027-28
item.description: Inzaghi emerges as Juventus option to replace Spalletti in 2027-28 La Gazzetta dello Sport reports that ex-Inter and Lazio coach Simone Inzaghi is a candidate to replace the Bianconeri’s coach in 2026-27. Luciano Spalletti is already under pressure as Juventus have had a slow start to the season, grabbing only 11 points in seven Serie A matches with three wins, two draws and two losses. VIGO, SPAIN – OCTOBER 15: Luciano Spalletti, Head Coach of Juventus, looks on before the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD2 match between Real Club Celta and Juventus at Estadio Balaidos on October 15, 2026 in Vigo, Spain. (Photo by Jose Manuel Alvarez Rey/Getty Images) Multiple sources claim that club directors and ownership are unwilling to replace Spalletti mid-season. The Tuscan tactician is under contract at the Allianz Stadium until 2028. NAPLES, ITALY – MAY 24: Antonio Conte SSC Napoli head coach greets his supporters after the Serie A match between SSC Napoli and Udinese Calcio at Stadio Diego Armando Maradona on May 24, 2026 in Naples, Italy. (Photo by Francesco Pecoraro/Getty Images) Their stance will inevitably change if results don’t improve over the next few months, prompting the Bianconeri to look to a caretaker coach, with Stefano Pioli and Antonio Conte emerging as potential replacements mid-season. However, if Spalletti finishes the season without reaching the minimum target, Champions League qualification, Juventus would look for a different type of coach. JEDDAH, SAUDI ARABIA – APRIL 13: Simone Inzaghi team Manager of Al Hilal FC during the AFC Champions League Elite game between Al Hilal FC and Al Sadd SC at Prince Abdullah AlFaisal Sports City on April 13, 2026 in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia. (Photo by Abdullah Ahmed/Getty Images) According to Gazzetta, former Inter manager Simone Inzaghi, currently in charge of Al-Hilal, is among Juventus’ leading candidates. The Italian coach, who guided Inter to the Serie A title in the 2023-24 season, is highly regarded for his top-flight experience, ability to develop players, and understanding of the club’s needs. During his time at Inter, Inzaghi also won the Coppa Italia twice, the Supercoppa Italiana three times, and reached the Champions League Final in 2023 and 2025.

Eze scored some spectacular goals in big moments when he was at Crystal Palace, including the winner in the FA Cup final against Manchester City in 2025. "I think all the high-end stuff that we saw from him which made him a player that Arsenal we're going to go and target, that's the icing on the cake," said Upson. "So when the foundation's not quite there in terms of the situations you're getting in and how quickly you get into the ball, where you are on the field, where your headspace is at about what your role is and what you've got to do, then it's hard to produce those moments that make you the top player." Eze shone from the left at Palace, but in his final two seasons in south London he operated from a narrower number 10 role. item.title: Barcelona reopen January transfer plans after PSG defeat exposes key weakness – report
item.description: Barcelona reopen January transfer plans after PSG defeat exposes key weakness – report Barcelona have reopened discussions about signing a defender in the January transfer window after their 4-2 Champions League defeat to Paris Saint-Germain exposed concerns about Hansi Flick’s defensive options. According to SPORT , the Catalan club is reconsidering the possibility of recruiting an experienced centre-back or full-back, although their restricted salary cap could complicate any move. The debate marks a potential change of direction after Barcelona opted against signing a central defender during the summer, despite Ronald Araujo’s departure on loan and Andreas Christensen’s persistent fitness problems. Barcelona reconsider defensive transfer strategy The defeat in Paris has intensified scrutiny of Barcelona’s defensive depth, with vulnerabilities across the back line allowing PSG to threaten repeatedly. Problems on the flanks and lapses in concentration at centre-back left Flick’s side exposed, while Joan Garcia’s saves helped prevent the scoreline from becoming even more damaging. For Barcelona, they know that their attacking quality can decide matches, but competing consistently in the Champions League also requires a defence capable of withstanding sustained pressure against top opponents like PSG. item.title: Vettel: First Ferrari contact long before joining Scuderia
item.description: FILE PHOTO - Sebastian Vettel of Scuderia Ferrari team stands in his pit box after the second free practice session during Formula 1 German Grand Prix. (is associated with: «Vettel: First Ferrari contact long before joining Scuderia») Fabian Sommer/dpa Sebastian Vettel has revealed that his first contact with Ferrari dated back to after his second Formula One title but that he turned the Scuderia down at the time because he was happy and successful at Red Bull. "The first contact came in 2012 after the second title," Vettel said in a documentary on him by public broadcasters ARD, titled "Being Sebastian Vettel." Vettel said it was a letter from then Ferrari president Luca di Montezemolo, simply congratulating him and "without referring to anything else." But Ferrari, looking to return to the winning ways they had enjoyed a few years earlier in the Michael Schumacher era, went a step further and Vettel said he had "a very secret meeting" with Di Montezemolo in which "he asked, what is the contractual situation, do you want to drive for Ferrari?" Vettel said he saw no reason for a move at the time, "so I turned them down, but of course I left the door open a little bit." Vettel won two more world titles with Red Bull in 2012 and 2013 but he eventually joined Ferrari in 2015 after a winless final season with Red Bull. He won 14 races for the Scuderia, from 53 top spots overall, but no world title and left after the 2020 season, retiring in 2022 after two seasons with Aston Martin. The four-part documentary available from Thursday also touches on the sacrifices his parents made to finance his racing career early on. "Of course I was aware that the financial situation was tense, that it wasn't easy when the next reminder notice arrived at home," Vettel said, adding that he felt a responsibility from his early karting days onwards to deliver. Vettel became the youngest world champion at age 23 in 2010. But he is set to lose this record to Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli, who is 20 and has a first chance to clinch the 2026 title on Sunday at the United States Grand Prix. Others appearing in the documentary include his former Red Bull mentor Helmut Marko and Lewis Hamilton, his long-time rival who became a friend because like him Vettel has interests beyond motor sports. Vettel talks about former German minister for economic affairs Robert Habeck from the Greens Party, based on Vettel's engagement for the environment and sustainability. The documentary starts with Vettel holding a non-F1 trophy, a rhino made of glass he received as Environmentalist of the Year in early 2026. “I believe that the path I have now begun to follow is sustainable in the sense that it brings me fulfilment,” Vettel said.

item.title: Scarlets wing Page tipped for huge Wales future
item.description: Macs Page made his 50th Scarlets appearance against Newcastle [Huw Evans Picture Agency] Macs Page has a "huge future" with Wales despite being left out of Steve Tandy's Nations Championship squad, according to former Dragons and Ospreys boss Lyn Jones. Wing Page, 21, had been tipped for a call-up for the November Tests having been in fine form for Scarlets. But Wales head coach Tandy instead opted to recall Rio Dyer and Gabriel Hamer-Webb alongside Josh Adams, Ellis Mee, Blair Murray, Tom Rogers and Louis Rees-Zammit. Tandy's squad features three uncapped players – prop Rhys Barratt, centre Aneurin Owen and scrum-half Che Hope – and Jones feels Page's age may have counted against him. "Experience is something that has been lacking from the Welsh squad," Jones told BBC Radio Wales Breakfast. "It's another young, uncapped player and he (Tandy) is probably a little bit afraid to introduce Macs just at the moment, but he has a huge, huge future for Wales. That is for certain." Having established himself at Parc y Scarlets in 2024-25, Page toured Japan with Wales in 2025 without winning a cap. He admits to enduring a more challenging second season with his region, but has made an impressive start to the current campaign. Former Wales flanker Jones says Crymych RFC product Page has been "one of the best players I have seen playing this season". Uncapped Dragons get Wales Nations Championship call Tandy on copping flak and his tough Wales calls "I don't wish to sound a bit over the top but he is," Jones added. "He has the ability to hold people up, take them on outside, [he is] unbelievably strong in the tackle area. "The big weakness with wingers in Wales is the inability to win the ball in the air from a high kick. It's been awful with us. With Macs Page, with Rio Dyer, it's a skill we are now starting to be at home with." Wales will take on Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff next month before meeting a southern hemisphere opponent on finals weekend at Twickenham. Page has travelled to South Africa with Scarlets for United Rugby Championship (URC) fixtures against Stormers and Bulls to finish the first block of the season.

item.title: The ‘troll-y’ reason Mina Kimes felt better about Patriots’ AJ Brown despite drops
item.description: David Butler II-Imagn Images The ‘troll-y’ reason Mina Kimes felt better about Patriots’ AJ Brown despite drops appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . New England Patriots fans were anticipating an AJ Brown eruption months before he even joined the team. They had all of training camp to gush over his newfound chemistry with MVP runner-up Drake Maye, leading up to a big Super Bowl rematch versus the Seattle Seahawks on NFL opening night. The star wide receiver hardly played a half with the Pats before suffering a high ankle sprain. Excitement was tempered, but it gradually built back up again. And then he competed against the New York Jets . Brown totaled three receptions on 10 targets for a meager 27 yards in a 26-19 divisional victory. Most memorably, the three-time Second-Team All-Pro posted two drops, including one that would have been a touchdown. All the hype and waiting, only to see him crash out in his Patriots home debut. Mina Kimes was actually encouraged , however. “I know this is going to sound troll-y, but I actually felt better about AJ Brown after watching the game, because he’s open the whole game,” the NFL analyst said on ESPN’s “NFL Live.” “I’m not worried about AJ Brown’s hands. That will be fine. I would be worried if AJ Brown wasn’t getting separation or if he looked slow, but he looked completely fine. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “He was winning consistently at the line of scrimmage… He just didn’t catch it for whatever reason, which is not something he has struggled with over the course of his career.” Drake Maye has been on a heater over the past three games 🔥 @danorlovsky7 and @minakimes discuss what has made the Patriots' offense so successful lately 🏈 pic.twitter.com/Jtbix3Jnf5 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) October 20, 2026 While some fans may instinctively roll their eyes, Kimes makes a compelling argument for a Brown bounce-back in this Thursday’s road matchup versus the Chicago Bears . The Super Bowl 59 champion owns an acceptable 5.7 percent drop rate across eight years, according to Pro Football Focus, so logic suggests he will be sharper in that area moving forward. Will the man stay healthy, though? Ankle injuries can linger, and playing twice in a five-day span after missing five weeks of action can be risky. AJ Brown is presently considered questionable after being a limited participant during Tuesday’s practice. If he does suit up in Chicago, fans will closely monitor his explosiveness and hands. Assuming Mina Kimes is right, though, it seems the Patriots may finally get the impactful playmaker they were yearning for all spring. item.title: Report: Liverpool are ‘not in any rush’ to extend the contract of their ‘most in-form player’
item.description: Report: Liverpool are ‘not in any rush’ to extend the contract of their ‘most in-form player’ Liverpool are ‘not in any rush’ to extend Alexis Mac Allister’s contract despite him being into the final two years of his current deal. The Argentine midfielder put the cat among the pigeons in early September when he said that he was ‘very sad’ at not being offered an extension at Anfield in the summer, unlike fellow 2023 signings Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch. The 27-year-old endured a slump in form last season but has been terrific in the first two months of this campaign, scoring twice in the Reds’ 4-3 win over Villarreal on Tuesday night and already just one goal off his entire haul from 2025/26. Liverpool in no rush over Mac Allister contract talks In an article for The Telegraph praising Mac Allister’s rejuvenation since the summer, Dominic King described the 2022 World Cup winner as the ‘catalyst’ for Liverpool’s comeback from 2-0 down last night and the ‘lynchpin’ of the Reds’ midfield. He concluded his article by stating that Anfield chiefs ‘are not in any rush to start talking about new contracts’ with the former Brighton man, but said that situation could change ‘if he keeps playing with this zip’. In a corresponding post on X , the journalist described Mac Allister as ‘the most important cog and most in-form player’ in Andoni Iraola’s squad, adding that he’s ‘playing with a point to prove’ after a poor 2025/26. (Photo by Dan Istitene/Getty Images) Want more Empire of the Kop coverage? Add us as a preferred source on Google to your favourites list for news you can trust Liverpool mustn’t let it drag out much longer While the midfielder has hinted that he’d like to extend his contract with Liverpool, it seems surprising that club chiefs haven’t been more proactive in ensuring that he stays at Anfield beyond the summer of 2028. Such a stance may have been understandable a few months ago, but as King says, the Argentine has again become one of his team’s most important players, setting the temp with his passing range and his knack for vital (and show-stopping) goals. Maybe sporting director Julian Ward will revisit the situation in the early weeks of 2027 once Mac Allister enters the final 18 months of his current deal and the balance of power begins to shift away from the Merseyside club. The midfielder will be 29 by the conclusion of his current terms, and Liverpool are often slow to hand signiifcant new deals to players in or approaching their 30s, hence why there may be a reluctance to pursure an extension for the Reds’ number 10 at present. If the Argentina maestro keeps performing like this, however, that must surely see contract talks become a priority so that the seemingly endless speculation over a move away will finally be quelled.

item.title: Jamie Carragher blown away by Man Utd star Youri Tielemans' NEW role
item.description: Leeds United v Manchester United - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Tactical tweak pays off for United Carragher has singled out Tielemans for widespread praise following United's hard-fought draw against Leeds on Sunday. The Belgium international produced a standout performance at Elland Road after manager Carrick altered his tactical setup. The visitors started the game brightly, with Tielemans deployed in a more advanced position than usual. He lined up alongside Bruno Fernandes and Bryan Mbeumo to form a dangerous attacking trio. This positional shift paid immediate dividends for the away side. Tielemans provided a precise pass in the final third to assist Mbeumo for the opening goal, before Dominic Calvert-Lewin eventually equalised for Leeds in the second half. Carragher highlights midfield vision and quality Carragher highlights midfield vision and quality The Belgian's vision and quality on the ball provided United with their best attacking moments of the match. His sharp awareness directly led to the opening goal, earning high praise from Carragher in the television studio. "The fact he scans and plays it on his backfoot means he can play it wide," Carragher explained on Sky Sports . "He knows Mbeumo is in that area and he knows he is going to find him. Absolute quality." Midfield energy helps unlock potential Tielemans has started all seven Premier League matches this season. However, his previous deep-lying partnership with Kobbie Mainoo had recently drawn heavy criticism from former club captain Gary Neville . With Mainoo currently sidelined through injury, Carrick opted to start Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos in central midfield. This injected much-needed energy into the middle of the park, providing a solid platform for the attackers. It also freed Tielemans from his heavy defensive responsibilities. "He’s scanning, looking over his left shoulder, looking where Bruno Fernandes is, looking where Bryan Mbeumo is," Carragher added. "Brilliant finish, but from Tielemans it was absolutely fantastic." Turning focus to European action Turning focus to European action The squad will now dust themselves down and prepare for a crucial European away trip. United are scheduled to face Como in the Champions League later this week. They will travel to Italy to play at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. Tielemans will be hoping to retain his advanced role as he looks to build on his impressive domestic showing.

item.title: Leicester to visit Oxford City in FA Cup first round
item.description: Leicester City won the FA Cup just five years ago but have since dropped down to League One [Shutterstock] Leicester City will travel to National League North side Oxford City in the 2026-27 FA Cup first round. It is the first time the Foxes have taken part at this stage of the competition since 2008 and they face sixth-tier opposition for a place in the second round. The 2021 winners were relegated to League One for this season with Russell Martin's side currently 14th having had an inconsistent start to the season. Meanwhile, there will be a family affair as Peterborough United face Reading as Posh boss Robbie Savage will take on his son Charlie's side when the first round kicks off around the weekend of Saturday, 7 November. A whopping 91 teams were named during the draw with four sides reaching the first round proper for the first time. Lowest-ranked team Tadley Calleva came from behind twice to force a replay with Aldershot but the ninth-tier outfit fell to a 2-0 defeat by the National League side on Tuesday to miss out on a trip to League One Barnsley. Eighth-tier Stafford Rangers stunned Gateshead 5-0 in their replay to set up a first round tie at home to Grimsby Town. AFC Rushden & Diamonds, also in the eighth tier, have won five games in the competition this season to reach the first round, with their reward a trip to League One side Burton Albion. item.title: RB Leipzig scout backs Yan Diomande to succeed at Real Madrid: ‘He will respond positively’
item.description: RB Leipzig scout backs Yan Diomande to succeed at Real Madrid: ‘He will respond positively’ Real Madrid have an opportunity to move ahead of Barcelona in the Champions League table when they take on RB Leipzig tonight. This promises to be a special game for Yan Diomande, who had joined Los Blancos in a €140 million deal from RB Leipzig in the summer. Speaking ahead of the encounter, the scout who first brought the Ivorian to Germany has backed him to flourish at the Bernabeu. The scout who spotted Diomande Rafa Gonzalez, Leipzig’s scout for Spain and Portugal for over a decade, revealed to AS how his eye for a player led him to the then-unknown teenager. Diomande was a huge hit at Leipzig. (Photo by Fran Santiago/Getty Images) A former goalkeeper who moved into scouting via spells in England and the United States, Gonzalez has overseen a string of shrewd calls, while admitting a few got away. The Diomande moment came at the Bernabeu in March 2025, when the youngster came on as an 86th-minute debutant for Leganes. “In my work, I rely heavily on my personal perceptions, and I immediately noticed qualities that everyone can now see in him, such as speed, intensity, audacity, effort, ball control, personality, defensive ability, and good tracking back,” he said. Gonzalez added that he grew fond of Diomande ten minutes into the game due to his special abilities. “It was only ten minutes on the field, but I loved him; I thought he was a very special player, and from then on, I began to follow him much more closely ,” he stated. Backing Diomande to succeed at Real Madrid Diomande has been on fire lately. (Photo by Mateo Villalba Sanchez/Getty Images) Despite the risk of paying €20 million for a player with barely any top-level minutes, Leipzig took the plunge, and the move paid off. Diomande ended up scoring 13 goals and mustering 10 assists in just 36 competitive matches, before joining Real Madrid for seven times the price. “I don’t consider myself primarily responsible for his signing because everyone in the group did their part to tie up all the loose ends. I did what was expected of me, but it was a team effort led by the sporting director ,” Gonzalez said. Finally, the Leipzig scout backed the Ivorian to succeed at Real Madrid. “ He will succeed in white. I’m convinced. He has talent, attitude, and room for improvement. The pressure is high, but with confidence, he will respond positively to the significant investment they’ve made ,” he concluded. After a slow start to the season, Diomande has certainly come into his own in recent matches, notably being involved in four goals in last three matches. It will be interesting to see whether or not he can continue that form against his former club tonight.

item.title: Official | PSG winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sustains right ACL tear
item.description: Official | PSG winger Khvicha Kvaratskhelia sustains right ACL tear PSG’s worst fears regarding Khvicha Kvaratskhelia’s (25) right knee injury have been unfortunately confirmed: the Georgian winger has sustained a rupture of the anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) in his right knee during Tuesday night’s home win against FC Barcelona for Matchday 3 of the UEFA Champions League. PSG report that Kvaratskhelia will undergo surgery in the coming days. Although Kvaratskhelia had a low-key start to the season with Les Parisiens , it is a considerable blow for Luis Enrique’s hopes of completing a three-peat in Europe’s premier club competition. Kvaratskhelia is set for an extended spell on the sidelines. No timeline has been set regarding his recovery period, but PSG can expect, at least, a six-month lay-off for Kvaratskhelia. GFFN | Bastien Cheval

item.title: Too much Overlap? Gary Neville’s podcast empire knows no bounds
item.description: The Overlap has gone daily, with Steven Gerrard and Joe Hart among the latest additions to an ever-growing family Viewed in 2026, Nathan Barley, Chris Morris’s 2005 sitcom, shows remarkable prescience about the last two decades of metropolitan life, from smartphone addiction and digital derangement to sheer existential vapidity. When Barley’s character referred to his occupation as “self-facilitating media node”, Morris and co-writer Charlie Brooker were way ahead on the creator economy. What the pair failed to predict was ex-footballers joining the sector in droves. These days, if you are a former footballer without a podcast or YouTube channel, then did you ever really play the game? Setting aside the Gary Lineker Goalhanger empire, manspreading its centrist-dad agenda into issues way beyond guffaws with Micah Richards and Alan Shearer, there is Gary Neville to rule them all. Manchesterism’s second-most influential practitioner has been on heavy manoeuvres. Unlike Lineker’s productions, the Overlap’s output continues to stick largely to football; a rugby podcast was mothballed in February, though its cricket equivalent continues. Continue reading...

item.description: Phil Foden shouted the loudest on a quiet night at the Etihad Stadium, announcing his personal return to form with an instinctive hat-trick as Manchester City dispatched AEK Athens with little fuss. Enzo Maresca had called for City to make their own noise amid the cacophony around the club but a businesslike victory in front of 20,000 fewer than watched the weekend’s win over Ipswich was required to get their Champions League back on track after suffering at the hands of Paris Saint-Germain . Those in attendance, officially 40,042 but that felt optimistic, saw Foden shine on the right wing and as a central striker, showing there is life without Erling Haaland, who watched from the bench. Admittedly, the opposition were not a match for the Premier League side, whose other goals came from Elliot Anderson and Rayan Cherki. Stavros Pilios’s consolation was more a reward for the boisterous fans in yellow and black, who created the atmosphere, than for the overall efforts of the visitors. Continue reading...

item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: Houthi conflict casts shadow as Saudi Arabia scales back sporting pipe dreams
item.description: A match delayed by missile attack warnings is not what Cristiano Ronaldo and co signed up for but it’s the new reality; the Saudi sporting juggernaut is stalling Cristiano Ronaldo grabbed the scarf in the colours of the Saudi Arabian flag and waved it at the sparse but enthusiastic crowd, who responded with rapturous cheers. It was a gesture of defiance rather than a victory salute, encapsulating the Saudi equivalent of “Keep calm and carry on”. Monday night’s Asian Champions League Elite game between Al-Nassr and the Uzbek side Neftchi Fergana had ended with a 3-1 win for the Saudi club coached by Ange Postecoglou, with Ronaldo, supported by Sadio Mané, scoring, the smattering of star names indicative of the lure of the Saudi Pro League. Yet this isn’t quite how Ronaldo and co would have anticipated life in Riyadh. The meagre attendance aside, Monday’s game was delayed by a threat of missile attacks from Yemen’s Houthi rebels. A safety warning issued 15 minutes before kick-off came two days after 13 people died and more than 300 were wounded by Houthi strikes on Riyadh’s King Khalid international airport. item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Guardiola returns to Manchester as City spin into dizzy mess against PSG
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! It is quite funny that PSG felt like the good guys at the Etihad Stadium but if we briefly detach ourselves from the notion that the European champions’ own sportswashing and cashsplashing has also done immeasurable damage to the beautiful game, then their 4-2 Bigger Cup shellacking of Manchester City was pure cinema, baby! I was stunned at reading the comments in support of Manchester City keeping their trophies, coming out of the mouth of their Bigger Cup rivals at PSG (yesterday’s Quote of the Day). Given the example of the organisers of the Tour de Lance … sorry, the Tour de France, this kind of ‘keep the awards you won’ stuff might get him sent to the Bastille. Or consider Formula One. They’ve got all kinds of rules about driver behaviour on the racetrack, and additional rules about what the crew can and cannot do to your car. Cars get inspected before each race, and there are also mandatory post-race inspections for every car. You might drive your car first across the line to the cheers of the crowd, but if the post-race inspection discovered that you cheated in how your team designed your vehicle, your memory of crossing the line is all you get to keep. Think about that for a minute. If the Premier League and Fifa cannot clear the bar for morals in sport set by the UCI and FIA, that says a lot. And none of it good” – Peter Rehwaldt. My friend Bernard grew up in Coventry. And as a boy he thought the team was called ‘Coventry City Nil’. I would get out more, but I’m a Manchester United fan” – Brendan Hughes. item.title: Robbie Savage the panto villain puts scepticism aside to leave Leicester reeling
item.description: Peterborough’s new boss has long been a divisive figure but a stunning 3-1 win at struggling former club offered a glimpse of his fearless philosophy It felt as though the stars had aligned when Robbie Savage’s first League One match in charge of Peterborough – his first EFL managerial role – happened to be at Leicester. He made his name here and forged a divisive and enduring reputation that has made him a permanent fixture in English football. Savage has long been a joker figure – an image born in his playing days, when he hurtled around midfield with long blond hair bouncing, launching into challenges that at one point made him the most booked player in Premier League history. A pantomime villain, a prankster and an eccentric who was once fined £10,000 by the Football Association – and two weeks’ wages by Leicester – for using the referee Graham Poll’s toilet before a match. (Savage blamed an upset stomach brought on by antibiotics). Continue reading...

item.title: The Premier League so far: draws, underperforming xG and other data pointers
item.description: Goal averages are crumbling as players take fewer touches in the box and forwards underperform against xG Goals are on the up in the Premier League. The average of 2.70 non-penalty goals per game in 2026-27 is higher than last season and two of the four previous campaigns. Yet we should have been even more royally entertained. Matches have averaged 2.88 non-penalty expected goals, the second most in the past six seasons. Chances have been going to waste. If the 20 teams converted at the par rate, there would have been almost two extra goals per week. As few as that sounds, the proportion of games drawn is higher than in any past Premier League season. Some tied matches might have been settled had the finishing been up to the mark. item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap .
